question.problem:
Compute $P(0<X<1)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}x(2-x),\, & 0\le x\le 2, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X<b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<X<1) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{4}x(2-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}-{x}^{2}+2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{[-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}([-\frac{1}{3}(1)^{3}+(1)^{2}]-[-\frac{1}{3}(0)^{3}+(0)^{2}]) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}([-\frac{1}{3}+1]-0) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot \frac{2}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
